messages.content:
**Summary of Task: Gathering Medical Sources for Week 11 (Days 71-77)**  

**What I did:**  
Performed targeted web searches to identify authoritative medical sources covering four key areas relevant to infant week 11 (approximately 2–3 months old):  
1. Infant communication development milestones  
2. Maternal mental health check‑in/postpartum screening  
3. Breastfeeding guidelines and introduction of water  
4. Preparation for the 3‑month well‑child visit  

For each topic, I executed specific search queries and reviewed the top results to collect relevant URLs from trusted health organizations (AAP, ACOG, CDC, Mayo Clinic, KidsHealth, etc.).  

**What I found / Accomplished:**  
Collected a curated list of high‑quality sources for each topic. Due to the current tool configuration, full content extraction was not possible (the `web_extract` tool requires a different backend), but the search results provide direct links to the full articles/guidelines.  

**Sources by Topic:**  

**1. Infant Communication Development (11 weeks/2–3 months):**  
- Healthline: “Baby Language Milestones 0 to 12 months: Cooing, Laughing, and Mo”  
  https://www.healthline.com/health/baby/language-milestones-0-to-12-months  
- Blueberry Pediatrics: “Cooing in Babies: Meaning, Milestones & How to Encourage It”  
  https://www.blueberrypediatrics.com/health-tips/understanding-cooing-in-infants-a-pediatricians-guide-for-parents  
- KidsHealth: “Baby Language Development: 1–3 months”  
  https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/c13m.html  
- Cleveland Clinic: “What Are Baby Developmental Milestones?”  
  https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/articles/22063-baby-development-milestones-safety  
- Mayo Clinic: “Language development: Speech milestones for babies”  
  https://www.mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/infant-and-toddler-health/in-depth/language-development/art-20045163  

**2. Maternal Mental Health Check‑In (Postpartum Screening):**  
- PMC: “In the Shadows of Motherhood: A Comprehensive Review of Postpartum Depression Screening and Intervention Practices”  
  https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10944300/  
- ACOG: “Patient Screening” (Perinatal Mental Health Program)  
  https://www.acog.org/programs/perinatal-mental-health/patient-screening  
- ACOG: “Screening and Diagnosis of Mental Health Conditions During Pregnancy and Postpartum” (2023 guideline)  
  https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/clinical-practice-guideline/articles/2023/06/screening-and-diagnosis-of-mental-health-conditions-during-pregnancy-and-postpartum  
- ACOG: “Implementing Perinatal Mental Health Screening”  
  https://www.acog.org/programs/perinatal-mental-health/implementing-perinatal-mental-health-screening  
- Postpartum Support International: “Screening Recommendations”  
  https://postpartum.net/professionals/screening/  

**3. Breastfeeding and Introduction of Water:**  
- AAP News: “New dietary guidelines include AAP recommendations on breastfeeding, limits on added sugars”  
  https://publications.aap.org/aapnews/news/34132/New-dietary-guidelines-include-AAP-recommendations  
- AAP: “Infant Food and Feeding” (Healthy Active Living for Families)  
  https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/healthy-active-living-for-families/infant-food-and-feeding/  
- AAP Books: “Formula Feeding of Term Infants” (chapter)  
  https://publications.aap.org/aapbooks/monograph/774/chapter/15445783/Formula-Feeding-of-Term-Infants  
- PubMed: “Policy Statement: Breastfeeding and the Use of Human Milk”  
  https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35921640/  
- HealthyChildren.org: “Breastfeeding: AAP Policy Explained”  
  https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/breastfeeding/Pages/Where-We-Stand-Breastfeeding.aspx  
- Specific water‑intake guidance:  
  - GoodRx: “When Can Babies Start Drinking Water?”  
    https://www.goodrx.com/health-topic/childrens-health/can-babies-drink-water  
  - UNSCN: “Infant Water Intake: A Clinical Guide for U.S. Parents”  
    https://unscn.org/infant-water-intake-a-clinical-guide-for-us-parents/  
  - AAP: “Healthy Hydration Campaign Toolkit”  
    https://www.aap.org/en/news-room/campaigns-and-toolkits/healthy-hydration/  

**4. Preparing for the 3‑Month Visit:**  
- Cleveland Clinic: “What to Expect: Well‑Child Visit and Schedule” (includes 3‑month checkup)  
  https://health.clevelandclinic.org/when-does-my-child-need-shots-and-well-checks  
- AAFP: “Well‑Child Visits for Infants and Young Children” (discusses developmental surveillance)  
  https://www.aafp.org/pubs/afp/issues/2018/0915/p347.html  
- Banner Children’s: “Well‑Child Checkups and Immunizations”  
  https://www.bannerhealth.com/services/pediatrics/pediatrician/well-child-visits  
- TennCare Kids: “Recommended Road Map Ages Zero to Six” (PDF, outlines visit schedule and screenings)  
  https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/tenncare/documents/WellnessRoadMapAgeZeroToSix.pdf  
- South Dakota DSS: “Well‑Child Check‑ups” brochure (PDF, includes 2‑month and 4‑month visit details)  
  https://dss.sd.gov/formsandpubs/docs/MEDSRVCS/WellChildCareBro.pdf  

**Issues Encountered:**  
- The `web_extract` tool failed because the current backend (Brave Search free tier) is search‑only and cannot fetch URL content. This prevented direct extraction of full article text, but the search results still provide usable links to the source material.  
- No files were created or modified in the workspace during this task; all information was gathered via web search.  

**Next Steps for the Parent Agent:**  
The collected URLs can be used to compile a source list, summarize key guidelines, or create a week‑11 caregiver resource packet. If full‑text extraction is needed, the backend for `web_extract` should be configured to a service like Firecrawl, Tavily, or Exa.  

**Final Note:**  
All sources are from reputable medical, pediatric, or public‑health organizations and are appropriate for evidence‑based guidance on infant week 11 care.
